rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command follows the gift of al-Kawthar as thanks: prayer honors God, while sacrifice benefits and shows compassion to creation; gratitude includes both worship and kindness to creatures.
rows.anchor: بعد أن بشر الله تعالى رسوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بإعطائه الكوثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer precedes sacrifice because it is a pillar, the first deed questioned, and a five-times-daily duty that remains obligatory in illness or poverty, whereas sacrifice depends on means.
rows.anchor: الصلاة أهم من النحر وهي ركن من أركان الإسلام وأول ما يسأل العبد عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an uses prayer differently by speaker: from God it is mercy, from the Prophet supplication, and from believers worship through words and actions.
rows.anchor: فهي إن كانت من الله تعالى فهي رحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whenever prayer and zakah appear together in the Qur'an, prayer comes first because it is more comprehensive and important.
rows.anchor: كلما ورد ذكر الصلاة والزكاة في القرآن تتقدم الصلاة على الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “for your Lord” makes prayer exclusive to God and contrasts with those who pray heedlessly for display in al-Ma'un.
rows.anchor: تفيد الاختصاص والقصد أن الصلاة لا تكون إلا لله وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing the Lord rather than saying “for us” avoids implying that prayer belongs to a benefactor; people thank the giver, while prayer belongs solely to God.
rows.anchor: الصلاة تكون للرب وليس للمعطي فإذا قال فصل لنا لأفاد أن الصلاة تكون للمعطي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from majestic plural “We gave you” to “your Lord” avoids suggesting partners or that the divine plural denotes multiple beings.
rows.anchor: إنا أعطيناك باستخدام ضمير التعظيم فلو قال فصل لنا لأوهم انه فيه شرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an pairs majestic-plural speech with singular language before or after it, affirming God's oneness and avoiding any implication of partners.
rows.anchor: لا يوجد موضع ذكر فيه ضمير التعظيم إلا سبقه أو تبعه إفراد بما يفيد وحدانية الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Your Lord” recalls the fulfilled promise in al-Duha; the author also observes that Qur'anic references to giving pair the gift with the Lord, who nurtures, gives, and governs.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية انجاز لما وعد الله تعالى رسوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في سورة الضحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nahr is specifically camel slaughter, whereas dhabḥ can describe slaughtering many animals; camels were prized Arab wealth, so the command calls for a valuable offering befitting the great gift.
rows.anchor: النحر في اللغة: يتعلق بنحر الإبل فقط ولا تستعمل مع غير الإبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Give charity” could be satisfied by a small gift, but nahr directs gratitude toward the best of one's wealth.
rows.anchor: الصدقة تشمل القليل والكثير فلو تصدق احدهم بدرهم أو بطير لكفى المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakah is unsuitable because the Prophet lacked the taxable minimum; it is annual and only 2.5 percent, a general duty rather than special thanks for al-Kawthar.
rows.anchor: الرسول - صلى الله عليه وسلم - لم يكن يملك النصاب للزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Udhiyyah could be fulfilled with a sheep and is restricted to four days, while the intended thanksgiving should not be limited to those days.
rows.anchor: الأضحية هي كل ما تصح به الأضحية الشرعية فلو ضحى بشاة لكفت

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes differed over whether the prayer and sacrifice mean Eid prayer, prayer generally, or a particular prayer; many read them generally, including Eid prayer and udhiyyah.
rows.anchor: الكثير من المفسرين قالوا إنها عامة ويدخل فيها صلاة العيد والأضحية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first “for your Lord” governs both commands by making the intended relation clear, so it need not be repeated after “sacrifice.”
rows.anchor: المتعلق الأول لربك كأنما يغني عن المتعلق الثاني وهو ما يسمى بظهور المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer's attachment to the Lord suffices because prayer is always worship, while slaughter can be for worship or food; repeating “for your Lord” could wrongly make every slaughter a ritual act.
rows.anchor: النحر فقد يكون إما للعبادة وقد يكون للأكل فقط وليست بهدف العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says “draw near” was not used because qurbān occurs only once in the Qur'an, in the story of Adam's two sons.
rows.anchor: القربان من التقرب ولقد ورد القربان مرة واحدة في القرآن الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah was revealed after the Prophet's two sons died and Quraysh called him cut off; a man whose sons die was called abtar.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية لما مات ابني الرسول - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقالت قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abtar can describe anything whose good effects cease, a man without surviving sons, or a loser.
rows.anchor: كل أمر انقطع من الخير أثره فهو أبتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite predicate with the detached pronoun confines “the abtar” specifically to the Prophet's hater, unlike an indefinite predicate that would mean merely one among the abtar.
rows.anchor: أراد الله تعالى أن يخصص الشانئ بالأبتر ولم يقل إن شانئك هو أبتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shanāʾān means hatred; the hater's mere dislike of the Prophet is ruin, even without openly declaring enmity, unlike the separate case of a believer among enemy people.
rows.anchor: جعل الله تعالى مجرد بغض الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers “shanīʾ” over “enemy” because bare hatred of the Prophet suffices for loss, even when hostility is not openly announced.
rows.anchor: لم يقل عدوك هو الأبتر لأن مجرد الشنئان للرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abtar, an afʿal descriptive adjective, conveys permanence like red, lame, brown, and bald; the author contrasts it with the temporary, changeable state conveyed by “mabtūr.”
rows.anchor: الأبتر صفة مشبهة على وزن أفعل تفيد الثبوت مثل الأحمر والأعرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The abtar's severance is lasting and may mean no descendants, or descendants who later accept Islam and cease praying for their unbelieving father, cutting off his remembrance and good.
rows.anchor: فاستخدام الأبتر وجب بكل معاني البتر مع استمرارية هذه الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report identifies the Prophet's hater as Abu Jahl, whose sons all accepted Islam and believed in God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: هو أبو جهل الذي اسلم أبناؤه كلهم وآمنوا بالله وبرسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not say God made the hater abtar: unlike the great gift of al-Kawthar, severance is presented as his original quality rather than an imposed change.
rows.anchor: الأبتر فهو ليس جعلاً إنما صفته الأصلية فهناك فرق بين جعل الإنسان بصفة معينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shanīʾak is especially forceful; a reported reading “shanʾak” intensifies the sense of being an extreme hater.
rows.anchor: في قراءة (شنئك) تفيد أن الأبتر هو الذي بالغ في الشنئ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending answers the opening: abundant good was given to the Prophet, while the hater is severed from every good and loses everything.
rows.anchor: ارتبط آخر السورة بأولها فالله تعالى أعطى في أولها الكثير من الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet loses neither this world nor the next and his name is continually remembered; the hater is the material and spiritual loser in both.
rows.anchor: الرسول - صلى الله عليه وسلم - لم يخسر لا في الدنيا ولا في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reports that God enabled the Prophet to slaughter a hundred camels after the command as thanks for His many blessings.
rows.anchor: مكنه من مئة من الإبل نحرها بعد نزول الآية شكراً لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two refuge surahs cover visible and hidden harms from outside or within: al-Falaq concerns unavoidable external evil outside moral responsibility, while al-Nas concerns inner harms a person can resist and is accountable for.
rows.anchor: سورة الفلق تضمنت الإستعاذة من الشرور الظاهرة والخفية الواقعة على الإنسان من الخارج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Falaq's unavoidable harms can earn patience and reward, whereas al-Nas's culpable harms are recorded as sins; exegetes call these the evils of afflictions and faults respectively.
rows.anchor: سورة الفلق استعاذة بالله من شرور المصائب وسورة الناس استعاذة بالله من شرور المعايب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʿūdhu means to turn to God for refuge and protection.
rows.anchor: أعوذ بالله: لغة هي بمعنى ألتجئ وأعتصم بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit command “say” is essential: it makes the supplicant personally voice and publicly acknowledge dependence on the Lord rather than leaving need unspoken.
rows.anchor: الأمر بالقول له أهمية كبيرة هنا ولو حذف الفعل لاختل المعنى المقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speaking one's need for help treats pride and may avert tyranny; the author links this to the warning that people transgress when they think themselves self-sufficient.
rows.anchor: قتل بل علاج للكبر والغرور الذي في نفس الإنسان والذي قد يودي به إلى الطغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God's protection is an act of obedience; awareness of needing divine aid softens hard hearts.
rows.anchor: إذا استعنا بالله ليعصمنا من الشرور فإنها من أسباب الطاعة له سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed couplet illustrates that a dignified person may willingly humble himself before his Lord.
rows.anchor: قالوا أتشكو إليه ما ليس يخفى عليه فقلت ربي يرضى ذل العزيز لديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One danger, satanic whispering, is met with refuge through three divine attributes; al-Falaq instead seeks refuge in one attribute from many evils, underscoring whispering's grave consequences.
rows.anchor: فالمستعاذ منه شر واحد والاستعاذة منه جاءت بالرب والملك والإله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order follows ordinary recourse: people first seek a knowledgeable guide (Lord), then authority (King), then God (Deity) when the other help fails.
rows.anchor: فالإنسان إذا وقع في حاجة يستعين أولاً بخبرته وعلمه أو بمن له خبرة وتجربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same sequence maps onto life and society: early life needs a caregiver, adulthood needs social order, and moral responsibility calls for the Deity; communities may obscure divinity through doubt or atheism.
rows.anchor: الأجنة هي البداية ثم يخرج الناس للحياة ليواجهوا المربي الذي يقدم لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attributes move from many to one: guides and nurturers may be numerous, kings fewer, but the Deity is one for everyone.
rows.anchor: تدرّجت الآيات من الكثرة إلى القلّة فالربّ هو المرشد الموجّه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “People” can mean one person, a small group, or everyone; its three repetitions specify different populations, expanding from a guide's dependents to a king's subjects to all humanity.
rows.anchor: كلمة " الناس " تُطلق على مجموعة قليلة من الناس أو واحد من الناس أو كل الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated noun cannot be replaced by a pronoun: that would make every description refer only to the Lord's initial group, losing the expanding referents.
rows.anchor: لذلك لا يغني الضمير هنا، بل لا بد من تكرار المضاف إليه مذكورا صريحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence of “people” reverses the attributes' count: the Lord's group is smallest, the King's larger, and the Deity's the largest.
rows.anchor: فناس المربي أقل، وناس الملك أكثر، وناس الإله هم الأكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no coordinating waw so the three titles do not imply distinct beings; they describe the one God as Lord, King, and Deity.
rows.anchor: ولم تأتي الآيات في السورة بواو العطف فيما بينها ولا يجوز أصلاً أن يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The refuge is from the evil of whisperers because jinn and humans include righteous as well as wicked members; unlike the wholly evil Satan, not all members of either group are evil.
rows.anchor: قد يكون الوسواس من الجنة أو من الناس فالجنة فيهم صالحون وفيهم قاسطون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites a report that one who mixes with people and patiently bears their harm is better than one who avoids them and cannot bear it.
rows.anchor: الذي يخالط الناس ويصبر على أذاهم خير ممن لا يخالطهم ولا يصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waswās uses the repeated faʿlāl pattern for repetition and hyperbole, unlike “the whisperer,” which does not itself convey intensity; the repeated sounds in kabkaba and hashasa illustrate the pattern.
rows.anchor: صيغة فعلال تفيد المبالغة أيضاً إذن كلمة وسواس تفيد المبالغة والتكرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking refuge from the whisperer's evil covers every harm the whisperer causes, whether or not it occurs through an actual whisper.
rows.anchor: الإستعاذة إنما تكون من كل شرور الوسواس سواء كانت وسوسة أو لم تكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khannās means one who hides and is an intensive form suggesting habitual withdrawal; people cannot kill the enduring devil, only seek God's refuge so its whisper retreats, or forget and fall into it.
rows.anchor: الخناس: صفة من (الخنوس) وهو الاختفاء، وهي أيضا صيغة مبالغة

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A hadith says Satan stays close to the human heart: he withdraws when God is remembered and whispers when God is forgotten.
rows.anchor: كما جاء في الحديث: الشيطان جاثم على قلب ابن آدم إن ذكر الله خنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says chests rather than hearts because the chest is wider and forms the entrances to the heart; whispering fills it and blocks the way for faith's inspirations.
rows.anchor: ذُكر في الآية مكان الوسوسة وهو الصدور ولم ترد القلوب لأن الصدور أوسع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans seek the Lord of people because people are the victims of whispering; jinn are its source, so they are mentioned first, and human whispering may originate with a jinn.
rows.anchor: الناس هم المعتدى عليهم ولذا جاء الآية رب الناس ولم يقل رب الجنة والناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn are named before humans because they are the original whisperers; the whispering affects human chests, not jinn chests.
rows.anchor: والجنة هم الأصل في الوسوسة، ولا تقع الوسوسة في صدورهم بل في صدور الإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In another verse, human devils precede jinn because the context concerns unbelieving humans who join jinn in whispering deceptive speech to one another.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأن السياق كان على كفرة الإنس الذين يشاركون الجن الوسوسة

none: فهرس ومحتويات الكتاب فقط، بلا شرح للآية.
